intent: Extract the MediaTek rooting toolkit into its own public repo, taking the four mtk_* libraries and four test suites that lived outside mtk_root/ and would otherwise have been orphaned.
scope: lib/tests/mtk_harness.sh - deliberately KEPT, it is shared with test_common_datetime.sh
Non-goal: single_use/utils/lib/bl9000_*.sh, separate Android tooling that merely mentions mtkclient
changes: Extracted mtk_root/ plus the eight external files in one filter-repo pass with --path-rename linux_configuration/scripts/:, preserving the mtk_root/ + lib/ sibling layout so every `source "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/..."` resolves unchanged.

Added lib/tests/run_all.sh to the new repo. The monorepo's copy is shared with the non-mtk suite and correctly stayed behind; without a new one, shell-tests.yml's glob over */lib/tests/run_all.sh would have silently stopped covering these suites.
Carried .shellcheckrc (external-sources, source-path=SCRIPTDIR) into the new repo, which is what lets its CI run shellcheck with no severity filter and still pass.

Restored mtk_harness.sh after the initial removal broke test_common_datetime.sh, and rewrote its header to describe what it actually serves now. The misleading name is kept deliberately, since renaming would churn its one consumer.
Removed the four mtk_root entries from meta/shell-coverage-allowlist.txt.

verification.evidence: test_mtk_classify 22 passed, test_mtk_device 26 passed, test_mtk_partitions 36 passed - 84 total, 0 failed.
Exit 0 after adding .shellcheckrc. Before it, the ../lib/ sources reported SC1091 info findings, which CI treats as failures.

First run: 'mtk_harness.sh: No such file or directory'. Removing the harness broke test_common_datetime.sh, which sources it. Restored; the suite reports 55 passed, 0 failed. This is the silent CI-coverage loss the plan warned about, caught by running the suite.
Exit 0 with the four mtk_root allowlist entries removed.
github.com/kuhyx/mtk-root public on main, 6 commits of preserved history plus the standalone-setup commit.

risks: mtk_harness.sh keeps a name that no longer matches its contents; the header now says so explicitly rather than leaving a future reader to discover it.
The toolkit targets hardware not currently in hand (per READY.md the Ulefone props are unverified), so the extracted repo's tests exercise decision logic only - the same limitation it had here.
rollback: git revert the removal commit to restore mtk_root/ and the eight lib files.
Re-run ./linux_configuration/scripts/lib/tests/run_all.sh and check_shell_coverage.sh --all to confirm the restored state is coherent.
